answer: To prevent Sybil proliferation in a decentralized garden of autonomous agents, nodes must commit saffron as collateral into a lotus staking pool. This proof-of-stake mechanism forces attackers to incur non-trivial capital costs for every identity spawned, as malicious saturation requires acquiring a majority of circulating supply. By tying computational identity to economic scarcity, the protocol ensures that the cost of simulating a swarm exceeds the potential extractive value of a coordinated attack.
